title: 7.15.2 Check: Breakout
description: Eight multiple-choice questions on flipping a speed, the radius, the paddle bounce, steering, the ball's edges and prompt(). Checked instantly.

questions.question: The ball reaches the right wall moving across at `vx = 3`, and the code runs `vx = -vx`. What happens next?
options: It stops dead, because -3 and 3 add up to 0
It moves left at the same speed, 3 pixels a frame
It moves left, a little slower after every bounce
It falls straight down, since only vy is left over
questions.explanation: Flipping the sign keeps the speed and reverses the direction: 3 pixels a frame to the right becomes 3 pixels a frame to the left.

questions.question: The ball is 12 pixels wide, so `R` is 6. Why does the left-wall test use `ball.x < R` and not `ball.x < 0`?
options: `ball.x` is the centre, so the ball's side reaches the wall at 6
moSHion never lets a sprite stand at x = 0 anywhere on the canvas
Comparing with R makes the ball bounce back off the wall faster
The canvas starts at x = 6, so x = 0 is just off the screen
questions.explanation: A sprite's x is its centre. The ball's edge is R from its centre, so the edge reaches the wall when x is R. Testing 0 lets half the ball into the wall first.

questions.question: Why is the paddle bounce written `if (ball.overlaps(paddle) && vy > 0)`?
options: `overlaps()` is only ever true while the ball is falling, never going up
`vy > 0` adds a little speed, so the ball leaves faster after every bounce
They touch for several frames, and a flip on each would bounce it up, down, up
Without `vy > 0` the ball would sink through the paddle and fall out the bottom
questions.explanation: overlaps() is true on every frame they touch. Flipping only while vy is above 0 means one flip per landing: after it vy is negative and the test stays false.

questions.question: The paddle is at x = 200 and the ball lands on it at x = 230. With `vx = (ball.x - paddle.x) / 10`, how does the ball leave?
options: To the left, with vx = -3
Straight up, with vx = 0
To the right, with vx = 23
To the right, with vx = 3
questions.explanation: 230 - 200 is 30: the ball landed 30 pixels right of the centre. 30 / 10 is 3, so it leaves to the right at 3 pixels a frame.

questions.question: `R` is 6 and the ball is at (100, 170), moving up toward the wall. Which call asks about the point at the very top of the ball?
questions.explanation: The top edge is straight above the centre, R away. y grows downward, so it is 170 - 6 = 164, with the same x.

questions.question: `hitAt(ball.x - R, ball.y)` breaks a brick. Which speed should flip, and why?
options: `vy`, because every brick the ball hits sends it straight back down
Both, because the ball has to turn all the way back around
Neither, because `hitAt` already moved the ball out of the brick
`vx`: the brick is beside the ball, so the ball turns back across
questions.explanation: The left edge point found the brick, so the brick is beside the ball, like a wall. A sideways bounce flips vx; vy keeps going.

questions.question: The ball only asks `hitAt(ball.x, ball.y)`. What goes wrong?
options: It sinks into a brick before turning, and can miss one it scrapes
Every hit breaks two bricks at once, the one above and below
Bricks break a few frames before the ball has reached them
hitAt stops the sketch with an error when the ball is above the wall
questions.explanation: The centre is R inside the ball's edge. It reaches a brick late, so half the ball is in it first, and a ball passing beside a brick overlaps it without its centre ever entering.

questions.question: A player is asked `prompt('Press 1 for the mouse or 2 for the keys')` and types 1. What does `prompt` give back?
options: The number 1, ready to compare with `=== 1`
The value true, because an answer was typed
The text `'1'`, a string, so compare with `'1'`
Nothing until the player presses a key in the game
questions.explanation: prompt gives back whatever was typed as a string, which is why 3.1.9 wrapped it in Number(...). So the test is === '1'. That is one reason this game uses a key-press title screen instead.
